_doc: THE SHARED QA CONTRACT. This file is byte-identical in patent-agent,
pulse-backend and pulse-frontend, and a test in each repo fails if they
diverge. Edit it in one repo and you must copy it to the other two in the
same change — that is the whole point: the three repos are separate git
repos, so nothing else keeps their vocabulary aligned.
JSON rather than YAML on purpose: patent-agent has no YAML parser and this
must be readable with zero dependencies in all three.
A test declares its tags in its name or via qa/cli.mjs metadata, e.g.
One corpus, sliced four ways. 'Run the security suite', 'run the inventor
journeys' and 'run everything touching ideas' are all the same filter.

areas._doc: Feature areas: the unit of 'is this relevant to my change'. Shared across all three repos so a backend diff can name a frontend test.

roles._doc: Journey actors. Mirrors UserRole in pulse-backend/prisma/schema.prisma; the drift test in pulse-backend asserts they match, so a new role cannot be added to the product without appearing here.

tiers._doc: What kind of claim a test makes. Where each runs is in the CI table in each repo's CLAUDE.md.

values.unit: Pure logic, no IO. policy.ts, review-chain.ts, scoring math.
values.contract: The API spec is current, has no breaking diff, and every adapter rule resolves to a real route.
values.behaviour: Declared state machines are complete AND enforced: legal transitions work, illegal ones are refused, no enum value is unreachable.
values.security: Authz matrix, IDOR, tenant isolation, payloads, headers, the privacy invariant.
values.journey: Role-driven feature loops end to end, across repo boundaries.
values.invariant: DOM geometry rules: overflow, clipping, overlap, unbounded lists, a11y.
values.conformance: ARIA + computed-style structure against the committed snapshot.

security._doc: Security concern tags. A test may carry more than one.

compliance._doc: Control references, so a CI artifact can be cited as evidence. Only tags that a test actually evidences from code — not aspirational.

soc2.CC6.1: Logical access controls restrict who may reach what.
soc2.CC6.2: Access is granted through a registration/authorisation process.
soc2.CC6.3: Access is modified and removed as roles change.
soc2.CC6.6: Access from outside the boundary is restricted.
soc2.CC6.7: Data in transit and at rest is protected; retention is bounded.
soc2.CC8.1: Changes are authorised, tested and approved before deployment.

gdpr.art5-1c: Data minimisation — only what is necessary is collected.
gdpr.art5-1e: Storage limitation — data is kept no longer than necessary.

values.smoke: One journey per role plus health. Target under 3 minutes.
values.pre-deploy: Everything that can run without a deployed build: unit, contract, behaviour, security-static.
values.post-deploy: journey + invariant + conformance against the deployed environment.
values.nightly: Every tagged test in the repo. The scanners and DAST are a SEPARATE, manual CI mode — see .gitlab-ci.yml — not part of this selection, because they are jobs rather than test files.

environments._doc: Browser tiers run against the deployed demo environment, by decision — an MR's code is not deployed anywhere, so E2E on an MR would test the previous release. E2E therefore runs post-deploy, nightly, and on demand.
environments._login_throttle: 5 logins / 5 min / IP. Log in ONCE per role and reuse storageState; do not log in per spec.
environments._writes: Journeys that mutate must namespace what they create with a run id and clean up in teardown. Demo carries real imported data.
